newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua says money needed to end property crisis.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua says money needed to end property crisis.

text.p: Nicaragua needs $500 million to resolve its nagging property problem and spark economic growth but does not have the cash to do it, Nicaragua's Vice President Enrique Bolanos said on Friday.

Bolanos told a news conference that the government, in the midst of a fiscal austerity programme, does not have the money needed to fulfil its plan to "buy the peace" in the property dispute and would probably have to raise it through taxes.

The government plans to resolve the dispute by giving legal titles to thousands of poor families who received confiscated property during the Sandinista's land reform while compensating the former owners. Wealthy Sandinistas who received confiscated properties will have to return it or pay market value to keep it, he said.
"This $500 million to pay for the properties they lost, which were taken by the poor, we call 'buying the peace'... God knows where it will come from," Bolanos said.
He warned that a failure to resolve the property problem would undermine Nicaragua's economic growth.
The dispute pits the occupants of more than 200,000 farms, houses and businesses confiscated during the 1979-1990 Sandinista government against the former owners who want their property returned.

The right-wing government of President Arnoldo Aleman held a series of talks with the opposition Sandinista Front in January to resolve the property dispute, but the talks fell apart at the end of February and remain deadlocked.
